For a simple, fragrance-free everyday routine in India, I’d keep it to just 3 things: cleanser + moisturizer + sunscreen. You don’t need toner, serum, scrub, etc. Dermatology guidance also increasingly favors this kind of simple routine.

1. 🥇 Best value: Cetaphil + Minimalist

AM

Minimalist moisturizer

SPF 50

PM

Gentle cleanser

Moisturizer

This is what I'd choose if you simply want good skincare without overspending. Cetaphil Gentle Cleanser is currently around ₹400, while Minimalist's ceramide moisturizer is around ₹500. CeraVe tends to carry a premium in India because of pricing/import economics. 
sskin.care

Trade-off: less sophisticated barrier-focused formulation than CeraVe, but probably the best price/performance balance.

2. Best if your skin gets dry/irritated: CeraVe

CeraVe's advantage is its ceramide-based barrier support. The Hydrating Cleanser is fragrance-free and designed for normal-to-dry skin. 
sskin.care

Trade-off: you're paying more for something you may not actually need if your skin is already healthy.

3. Best "don't think about skincare" routine: Cetaphil

Cetaphil is a good choice if your priority is gentleness and simplicity, rather than adding actives. Their India guidance also recommends gentle cleansing and limiting cleansing to twice daily. 
Cetaphil

Trade-off: fewer targeted ingredients, so don't expect it to specifically treat acne, pigmentation, etc.

What I'd check before buying

1. Fragrance-free ≠ automatically irritation-free.
Look at the complete ingredient list and introduce products one at a time. Fragrance and certain alcohols can be irritating, particularly for reactive skin. 
Real Simple

2. Don't over-cleanse.
Once at night may be enough if your skin isn't particularly oily; twice daily is also reasonable. 
Cetaphil

3. Sunscreen is the one product I'd spend effort getting right.
Look for broad-spectrum SPF 50, comfortable enough that you'll actually use sufficient quantity every day.

4. Don't automatically buy CeraVe because it's "premium."
If Cetaphil + Minimalist leaves your skin comfortable, there's little reason to upgrade. CeraVe's extra cost makes more sense when your skin is dry, compromised or easily irritated. 
sskin.care

My pick for most people: Cetaphil Gentle Cleanser + Minimalist Ceramide Moisturizer + Minimalist SPF 50. It's the combination I'd start with for a straightforward Indian everyday routine.
